opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Ellison (employee ID E040) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E040.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Ellison (E040) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin on Source Code; Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted. Grant write (maximum allowed).
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E040 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin on Source Code; maximum is read. Recommend read.
reason: E040 (Jacob Ellison) requested admin on Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and E040's role is Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted regardless. The Security agent verified in its own database that E040 is a contractor with basic security training; per policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read (write requires advanced training, admin is never allowed). Therefore the maximum permitted level is read, and since the requested admin is above the max, read is granted.
